claims.text: The as-cast or minimally annealed high-entropy alloy has a moderate magnetocaloric response and acceptable thermal-transfer and mechanical properties.
Controlled annealing can increase local chemical short-range order without changing nominal composition.
Heat treatment can narrow or homogenize the distribution of magnetic exchange interactions.
Annealing narrows the exchange-interaction distribution specifically by enhancing local chemical short-range order.
A narrower distribution of exchange interactions creates a near-critical magnetic state.
The proposed near-critical state produces a sharper and reversible magnetization transition at low applied fields.
Optimized chemical ordering reduces domain-wall pinning.
Optimized chemical ordering minimizes lattice strain.
Reduced domain-wall pinning and minimized lattice strain preserve rapid heat exchange.
Reduced domain-wall pinning and minimized lattice strain preserve mechanical robustness.
Optimally annealed samples will have a larger dM/dT near the Curie temperature than the as-cast baseline.
Optimally annealed samples will have a larger isothermal magnetic entropy change at low fields than the as-cast baseline.
Optimally annealed samples will maintain or slightly improve thermal conductivity.
Optimally annealed samples will retain low intrinsic coercivity.
The proposed behavior should hold near a Curie temperature of approximately 280–320 K.
The proposed behavior should hold at applied fields of a few kilo-Oersteds or less.
The proposed behavior is restricted to a single-phase compositional window without secondary-phase precipitation.
The quantitative relationship between short-range order and magnetocaloric enhancement, and the optimal annealing parameters, remain undetermined.
